17938-contrary-mary.title: Contrary Mary
17938-contrary-mary.creator: Temple Bailey
17938-contrary-mary.description: A book by Temple Bailey. Remembers a Face and Delilah Remembers a Voice; and in Which a Poem and a Pussy Cat Play an Important Part. CHAPTER VI In Which Mary Brings Christmas to the Tower Rooms, and in Which Roger Declines a Privilege for Which Porter Pleads. CHAPTER VII In Which Aunt Frances Speaks of Matrimony as a Fixed Institution and is Met by Flaming Arguments; and in Which a Strange Voice Sings Upon the Stairs.

32752-to-lhassa-at-last.title: To Lhassa At Last
32752-to-lhassa-at-last.creator: Unknown
32752-to-lhassa-at-last.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It really was rather nice. It had been quite hot in the plains, and was pleasantly cool up here. My wife and family had preceded me and had been settled for some weeks in the house which we had taken in the hills for the hot weather, and now I had just arrived on two months' leave.

arxiv-2005-03559.title: Asymptotic safety and quantum gravity amplitudes Journal: Nuclear Physics B
arxiv-2005-03559.creator: Jan H. Kwapisz, Krzysztof A. Meissner
arxiv-2005-03559.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Jan H. Kwapisz, Krzysztof A. Meissner. Application of the Weinberg’s conditions of asymptotic safety to amplitudes and not to couplings of the effective action can help to uniquely define the running in the UV and avoid some of the asymptotic safety program problems. As it turns out the requirement for a quantum gravity to be defined by S-matrix, that obeys the Weinbergs asymptotic safety criteria is a very restrictive one. The idea is illustrated by the 4-graviton amplitude in string theory and its symmetries.

arxiv-2104-08312.title: Data Shapley Valuation for Efficient Batch Active Learning
arxiv-2104-08312.creator: Amirata Ghorbani, James Zou, Andre Esteva
arxiv-2104-08312.description: Abstract Annotating the right set of data amongst all available data points is a key challenge in many machine learning applications. Batch active learning is a popular approach to address this, in which batches of unlabeled data points are selected for annotation, while an underlying learning algorithm gets subsequently updated.

arxiv-2108-08231.title: Non-Hysteretic Condition in Negative Capacitance Junctionless FETs
arxiv-2108-08231.creator: Amin Rassekh, Farzan Jazaeri, Jean-Michel Sallese
arxiv-2108-08231.description: Abstract This paper analyzes the design space stability of negative capacitance double gate junctionless FETs (NCDG JLFET). Using analytical expressions derived from a charge-based model, we predict instability condition, hysteresis voltage, and critical thickness of the ferroelectric layers giving rise to the negative capacitance behavior. The impact of the technological parameters is investigated in order to ensure hysteresis-free operation.

arxiv-2210-08125.title: Accretion Induced Collapse of White Dwarfs as an Alternative Symbiotic Channel to Millisecond Pulsars
arxiv-2210-08125.description: Abstract Recently, extra motivation has been given to the investigations of an unresolved problem of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) produced by the recycling process, as an apparent role of the accretion-induced collapse (AIC) in white dwarfs (WDs) was suggested to this concern.

arxiv-2503-22795.title: The Eras Tour: Mapping the Eras of Taylor Swift to the Cosmological Eras of the Universe
arxiv-2503-22795.creator: Jane C. Bright
arxiv-2503-22795.description: Abstract This paper explores an unexpected yet compelling parallel between the evolution of the universe, as described by cosmological eras, and the artistic evolution of Taylor Swift, delineated by her distinct album eras. By mapping key characteristics and transitions in the universe’s history to corresponding themes and milestones in Swift’s career, I offer a novel perspective on both.

arxiv-2504-08161.title: Rethinking the Foundations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2504-08161.creator: Michael Bowling, Esraa Elelimy
arxiv-2504-08161.description: Abstract Algorithms and approaches for continual reinforcement learning have gained increasing attention. Much of this early progress rests on the foundations and standard practices of traditional reinforcement learning, without questioning if they are well-suited to the challenges of continual learning agents.

arxiv-2508-16571.title: LLM-Based Agents for Competitive Landscape Mapping in Drug Asset Due Diligence
arxiv-2508-16571.creator: Alisa Vinogradova, Vlad Vinogradov, Dmitrii Radkevich, Ilya Yasny, Dmitry Kobyzev
arxiv-2508-16571.description: Abstract In this paper, we describe and benchmark a competitor-discovery component used within an agentic AI system for fast drug asset due diligence. A competitor-discovery AI agent, given an indication, retrieves all drugs comprising the competitive landscape of that indication and extracts canonical attributes for these drugs.

plos-pone-0005772.creator: Mercedes Montero-Balaguer, Kendra Swirsding, Fabrizio Orsenigo et al.
plos-pone-0005772.description: PLOS ONE research article. VE-cadherin is an endothelial specific, transmembrane protein, that clusters at adherens junctions where it promotes homotypic cell-cell adhesion. VE-cadherin null mutation in the mouse results in early fetal lethality due to altered vascular development. However, the mechanism o

pmc-10545627.title: Tau protein spreads through functionally connected neurons in Alzheimer’s disease: a combined MEG/PET study
pmc-10545627.creator: Deborah N Schoonhoven, Emma M Coomans, Ana P Millán, Anne M van Nifterick, Denise Visser, Rik Ossenkoppele, Hayel Tuncel, Wiesje M van der Flier, Sandeep S V Golla, Philip Scheltens, Arjan Hillebrand, Bart N M van Berckel, Cornelis J Stam, Alida A Gouw
pmc-10545627.description: Recent studies on Alzheimer’s disease (AD) suggest that tau proteins spread through the brain following neuronal connections. Several mechanisms could be involved in this process: spreading between brain regions that interact strongly (functional connectivity); through the pattern of anatomical connections (structural connectivity); or simple diffusion.

pmc-11294359.title: Effects of Baduanjin Exercise on lung function and 6 min walk in COPD patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11294359.creator: Feiyun Song, Kexin Ding, Wei Qi, Wen Sun, Heping Xiang, Mingyun Sun, Rui Xia
pmc-11294359.description: COPD is a public health problem of global concern, which seriously affects the quality of life of patients and is also the third leading cause of death from non-communicable diseases. To investigate the effect of Ba duan jin exercise on lung function and the results of a 6-min walking trial in patients with stable COPD.

pmc-11530253.title: Lowering the Carbon Footprint Through Telehealth Vasectomy Consults: A Retrospective Observational Study
pmc-11530253.creator: Paul J Wurtz, Emma Harwood, Thomas E Schroeder, Christopher M Deibert
pmc-11530253.description: Objective: This study aimed to quantify the impact of shifting in-person pre-vasectomy consultations to telehealth visits on travel time and carbon footprint reduction.Materials and methods: Utilizing retrospective chart analysis, we examined men who underwent vasectomy at our institution from November 15, 2020, to November 15, 2021.

pmc-11639358.title: Optimal configuration of hydrogen storage capacity of hybrid microgrid considering peak regulation and frequency modulation requirements
pmc-11639358.creator: Dan Yu, Yuhan Guo, Weijun Zhu
pmc-11639358.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study proposes an innovative hydrogen storage capacity optimization configuration method that considers multiple demand factors, addressing the issue that traditional methods for optimizing hydrogen storage capacity in hybrid microgrids cannot simultaneously balance economic efficiency and grid connection quality.

pmc-12533758.title: Revisiting strategies to target ABC transporter-mediated drug resistance in CNS cancer
pmc-12533758.creator: Haneen Amawi, Alaa M. Hammad, F. Scott Hall, Noor Hussein, Aseel O. Rataan, Abeer Mrayyan, Taqwa Al-kofahi, Ali Hmedat, Charles R. Ashby, Amit K. Tiwari
pmc-12533758.description: A significant number of anticancer drugs fail to treat primary and metastatic brain tumors primarily because of the complex blood-brain barrier (BBB) and overexpression of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters, which decrease drug penetration into the central nervous system and ultimately into tumors.

pmc-12609387.title: Microbial Biotransformation of Chicory by Bacteroides fragilis: In Vitro Implications for Obesity-Related Psoriasis
pmc-12609387.creator: Arthur Chervet, Rawan Nehme, Clemence Defois-Fraysse, Caroline Decombat, Celine Auxenfans, Bertrand Evrard, Solene Michel, Edith Filaire, Jean-Yves Berthon, Assia Dreux-Zigha, Laetitia Delort, Florence Caldefie-Chezet
pmc-12609387.description: Obesity, a global health crisis, is linked to chronic low-grade inflammation and an increased risk of developing various chronic diseases, including psoriasis. Probiotics, postbiotics, and fermented foods have shown promise in combating inflammation and obesity. This study aimed to develop and characterize a chicory extract fermented with Bacteroides fragilis (C-B.

pmc-12709021.title: Challenges Related to Overcoming Addiction: Assessing Motivation and Readiness to Quit or Reduce Cigarette Smoking
pmc-12709021.creator: Natalia Miller, Piotr Samel-Kowalik, Bolesław Samoliński
pmc-12709021.description: IntroductionThe life expectancy of a cigarette smoker is reduced by an average of 10 years as a result of smoking, although this effect may be mitigated by timely cessation. It has been proven that smoking cessation is beneficial to health regardless of comorbidities and age.

pmc-13136763.title: Cultural adaptation and validation of the Arabic version of the Fear of Cancer Scale
pmc-13136763.creator: Raghib Abusaris, Dimah Alsaqabi, Alyaa FA Ibrahim, Ashraf A’aqoulah, Mona Alanazi, Manal Alsheikh, Fai Albawardi, Mohammed Awawdeh, Samah Saad Salem
pmc-13136763.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the Arabic version of the Fear of Cancer Scale.MethodsThe study was conducted via an online survey across all regions of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, using a cross-sectional validation design. A non-probability consecutive sampling method was used to recruit 71 non-cancer adults aged 18 years or older.

pmc-13195782.title: An upper limb stroke rehabilitation exercise video dataset
pmc-13195782.creator: S. Nandana, M. Thenmozhi Dharshini, Vismaya Viswanathan, Binoy B. Nair
pmc-13195782.description: Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide with a disproportionately high burden in low and middle-income countries. In such countries, limited access to rehabilitation centres, shortage of trained physiotherapists and socioeconomic constraints impede continuous post-stroke care resulting in poorer recovery. Telerehabilitation has emerged as a scalable and cost-effective solution enabling remote monitoring and therapy personalization.

pmc-13273224.title: Acute toxicity assessment and metabolomic profiling of Taxus sumatrana leaf extract as a sustainable alternative to bark harvesting
pmc-13273224.creator: Pamungkas Rizki Ferdian, Wanda Kuswanda, Hadi Sukardi Alikodra, Herjuno Ari Nugroho, Haidir, Ni Luh Putu Rischa Phadmacanty, Ardya Widyastuti, Rizki Rabeca Elfirta, Rini Madyastuti Purwono, Asep Hidayat, Yani Silfariani, Alif Zikri Fadhali
pmc-13273224.description: Taxus sumatrana (Taxaceae) is an Indonesian endemic species known for its anticancer activity due to taxane derivatives. Despite its pharmacological importance, T. sumatrana remains underexplored, and its populations are increasingly threatened by extensive bark harvesting, compromising the tree’s natural defence system and often leads to stem rot and mortality.

pmc-13395955.title: Quantifying the Role of Longitudinal Chromatic Aberration and Age in Night Vision Disturbances
pmc-13395955.creator: Laura Clavé, Maria S. Millan, Laia Salido, Miguel Faria-Ribeiro, José M. González Méijome

pmc-13472724.title: Nocturnal polygraphy in neuromuscular disorders: is it a useful diagnostic tool?
pmc-13472724.creator: Aleciane Cristine de Oliveira, Thayanne dos Santos Corrêa, Lucas Figueira Vieira, Iago Resende Carvalho, Daniela Name Chaul, Ana Elizabeth Cunha Guimarães de Almeida, Vitor Laguardia Guido Faria, Paulo Cézar Simamoto Júnior, José Fausto de Morais, Fernando Gustavo Stelzer, Isabela Maria Bernardes Go
pmc-13472724.description: BackgroundPatients with neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) have a high incidence of sleep-related breathing disorders. These include obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), which is characterized by recurrent episodes of upper airway obstruction during sleep, resulting in intermittent hypoxemia and sleep fragmentation. Obstructive sleep apnea may be more common in patients with NMDs than in the general population.

pmc-13531308.title: Patient, family member and healthcare professionals’ experiences of physiotherapy airway clearance techniques during hospital admission: a scoping review
pmc-13531308.creator: Kirsty Jerrard, Rhian Dowding, Brenda O'Neill, Judy M. Bradley, Bronwen Connolly
pmc-13531308.description: IntroductionEffective secretion management is crucial for hospitalised patients with retained secretions due to critical illness, chronic respiratory disease or infection. Airway clearance techniques (ACT), primarily physiotherapist-delivered and advocated in guidelines, support secretion removal. However, limited knowledge exists regarding the experiences of patients, family members and healthcare professionals involved in ACT.
